summary: Discovery call focused on Aperture's plan to migrate inference workloads from OpenAI to a Dedicated/Private deployment. Main concerns: eval parity, latency/cost tradeoffs, compatibility with vLLM/TGI tooling, and security (KMS/SOC2). Next steps: pricing, benchmarks, share security docs, schedule POC kickoff.
topics: deployment options: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
transcript:
[00:00] Samira: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Samira from Redwood, accounts lead — with me is Jonas, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:10] Maya: Good, thanks. Maya here — VP of ML at Aperture. We, uh, we've been running most inference on OpenAI but costs have been spiking and we want more control.
[00:18] Liam: Hey, Liam — platform eng. We're evaluating Dedicated or maybe Private because of data residency and throughput needs.
[00:24] Priya: Priya, SecOps — I mainly want to understand encryption, audit logs, and how keys are managed.
[00:32] Jonas: Great, thanks. Quick agenda: understand current stack, workloads and SLAs, talk about migration path and compatibility, then POC/benchmarks. Sound good?
[00:40] Maya: Yep. Quick background: we're a ML infra team for real-time personalization, 200ms SLO for top-1 response, currently using OpenAI gpt-4o-ish for ranking and generation in some places, and Anthropic for safety checks. We also run some self-hosted models with vLLM for cost-sensitive workloads.
[00:58] Samira: OK, sounds like a mixed deployment today. Can you share rough qps and token volumes?
[01:06] Maya: Sure, peak qps around 120 across services, average tokens per request 450. Monthly tokens — I don't have exact but ballpark 1.2B tokens. Costs have gone up, so looking at Dedicated to get predictable pricing.
[01:20] Jonas: And latency SLO is 200ms — is that p50 or p95?
[01:23] Maya: p95. P50 can be lower, but p95 is what product measures.
[01:29] Jonas: Good — that helps. A couple of typical migration questions we get: eval parity (do outputs match OpenAI), runtime compatibility (can you reuse vLLM/TGI tooling), and of course security (KMS, VPC). Which of these is the biggest blocker for you?
[01:45] Liam: Eval parity is big. We have a large eval corpus and we need model/response parity or at least predictable delta so downstream models don't break. Also how easy is it to switch routing between Hosted and Dedicated?
[01:56] Samira: Right, Redwood supports model variants and smart routing; you can pin versions and do canaries. Jonas, do you want to speak to parity and evals?
[02:05] Jonas: Yeah. So, in our experience, exact token-level parity with OpenAI is often not possible if you're switching model families; but for open model variants we provide Redwood-verified performance and we do prompt tuning guidance to get behavior close. We also run side-by-side eval harnesses — we can run your eval suite against candidate models and surface regression deltas.
[02:24] Maya: How long does that take and what's involved?
[02:27] Jonas: Typical turnaround for initial evals is 2–3 business days if you give us your eval set and sample prompts — we run against two to three model candidates. For POC we can run larger sweeps but that takes longer. We'll share the benchmark harness link.
[02:39] Priya: On the security front — SOC2 is required, we need audit logs for inference requests, and customer-managed KMS. Do you support HSM-backed keys and per-tenant key separation?
[02:50] Jonas: Yes, Dedicated and Private support KMS integrations; Private can be deployed with customer-managed HSM. For Hosted we offer encryption at rest with provider-managed keys by default and bring-your-own-key for Dedicated tiers. Audit logs are available in Redwood Console with token-level traces.
[03:05] Priya: Also need data residency — some records must remain in eu-west-1. Can Dedicated guarantee region-specific tenancy?
[03:12] Samira: Dedicated can be provisioned in target regions and we support region pinning; Private on-prem is of course fully local. We'll capture residency requirements in the POC scope.
[03:21] Liam: About tooling — we run vLLM with some custom kernels and a TGI-based path for a few models. Can you run our existing converters or do we need to retrain?
[03:31] Jonas: We support common model formats; Redwood runtime has kernel selection and supports optimized kernels. For vLLM/TGI users we often recommend quantized variants we host, and we can accept your model artifacts if licensing allows. There may be small changes in perf; we do a compatibility run.
[03:44] Maya: Licensing is a question — some upstream models can't be redistributed. How does Redwood handle models that we already have licenses for?
[03:51] Jonas: If you have licensed model files, Private deployment is the cleanest—bring the model, we run the control plane or you host full stack. For Dedicated we can discuss contractual arrangements; sometimes we host a customer-provided model under strict entitlements. We'll flag legal for that.
[04:05] Maya: Good to know. Can we talk latency tradeoffs — your Dedicated latency vs current OpenAI p95?
[04:11] Jonas: Typical Dedicated p95 depends heavily on instance type and batching. For single-request 450-token payloads, on our 8xA100 class nodes configured for low-latency we often see 120–180ms p95 for models similar to Llama-3-70b-chat quantized paths. But that's a rough number, and your actual workload and prompt length matter. We should do a workload-matched benchmark.
[04:33] Liam: And how does batching affect p95? If we accept micro-batching to lower cost, will we breach 200ms?
[04:40] Jonas: There's a tradeoff. Intelligent batching can cut cost by 20–50% but increases tail latency — Redwood lets you configure per-route policies. You can set strict latency SLOs with lower batching for critical paths and enable batching for background workloads.
[04:55] Maya: For eval parity, could we run both systems in parallel and route a percentage of traffic to Redwood to validate regressions?
[05:01] Samira: Absolutely — we recommend canary routing and A/B tests. We'll help with rollout policies and metric hooks to validate quality.
[05:09] Priya: What about request-level PII redaction? We have GDPR needs and need to redact or never store certain tokens.
[05:16] Jonas: You can configure retention policies per-route; Dedicated/Private give you options to disable request logging or redact tokens before persisting. We also support on-the-fly masking via our pre-processing hooks.
[05:29] Maya: Operationally, what's the support SLAs for Dedicated? We need on-call escalation.
[05:34] Samira: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; enterprise add-on gives 24/7 on-call and a named TAM. We'll include support tiers in the pricing doc.
[05:44] Liam: Let's dig technical: our infra runs k8s, we currently orchestrate vLLM instances with custom sidecars. For Private, what's needed to deploy Redwood?
[05:53] Jonas: Private can be deployed as a customer-controlled control plane with options for on-prem. We provide deployment manifests that integrate with k8s and your networking. For the on-prem package we have a setup guide; infra usually spends 1–3 weeks for initial deployment depending on security reviews.
[06:09] Maya: Cost modeling — if we move to Dedicated, how predictable is price with variable qps?
[06:16] Samira: Dedicated is reserved capacity with commit tiers; you pay for reserved GPU pools and get predictable per-token economics. We also have burst capacity options for spiky traffic. We'll illustrate with a pricing SKU and sample calc.
[06:28] Priya: Can you break down token-level cost including egress and storage?
[06:33] Samira: Yes, pricing doc includes compute per-token plus storage and egress estimates; we'll put a sample calc for your volumes.
[06:40] Maya: One of our concerns is regression detection — do you provide eval dashboards that show per-prompt deltas?
[06:47] Jonas: Redwood Optimize includes quality monitoring; we can hook your eval set to trigger regression alerts and show per-prompt diffs and metrics. It's part of the console.
[06:58] Liam: About integration: do you expose the same API semantics as OpenAI so app layer changes are minimal?
[07:04] Jonas: Our API is similar but not identical; we provide SDKs and an OpenAI-compat layer for common endpoints. For most apps it's small changes. We also support function calling and streaming.
[07:15] Maya: Great. For POC, what's a minimal scope to validate parity and latency?
[07:20] Jonas: Minimal POC: 1) Provide your eval corpus and 1000 production-like requests, 2) We run side-by-side on your chosen model flavors for 72 hours, 3) We run perf tests at targeted qps (e.g., 50 qps) and collect p95/p99. That should be enough to validate.
[07:36] Samira: We'll send a POC checklist and the benchmark harness link after the call.
[07:41] Priya: For audit logs, can logs be forwarded to our SIEM or S3 bucket?
[07:46] Jonas: Yes — we support log forwarding to customer S3, CloudWatch, or a syslog endpoint. We can also provide filtered anonymized logs.
[07:55] Maya: On the note of model hosting — we have some custom fine-tuned models on top of Llama family. Can Redwood host fine-tuned weights?
[08:04] Jonas: We can host fine-tuned models; depending on license you may bring the artifacts. For hosted Dedicated we manage weights; for Private you keep them on prem. We'll need to validate format compatibility.
[08:16] Liam: Any customers who migrated from OpenAI to Dedicated with similar profiles?
[08:21] Samira: Yes — a few mid-market SaaS companies in personalization migrated last year. We have an anonymized case study; I'll share it.
[08:29] Maya: Please do.
[08:31] Jonas: Quick follow-up question — do you use function calling heavily? That affects latency a bit.
[08:36] Maya: Yes, we've added function calls for structured outputs in some pipelines.
[08:40] Jonas: Good to know — we'll ensure the POC includes function call scenarios.
[08:45] Priya: Compliance: any SOC2 cert number we can reference?
[08:48] Samira: We'll share our SOC2 Type II report with NDA; Jonas, include the link to security pack.
[08:55] Jonas: Will do.
[09:00] Maya: Wanted to clarify routing — can we do hybrid: some routes to OpenAI hosted, others to Redwood Dedicated, with split by route?
[09:08] Jonas: Yes, routing by policy is supported. You can route on user, tenant, or route name, and set fallbacks.
[09:16] Liam: For the benchmark, we need to simulate session-based KV cache usage because we use a lot of context caching. Can you emulate that?
[09:24] Jonas: Yes, we can run the cache-hit patterns; we'll want a sample of session traces to model it.
[09:30] Maya: Ok let's talk timeline. If we start POC week of 4/20, what's the target to make a decision?
[09:36] Liam: Tech decision in 3–4 weeks post-POC, procurement later.
[09:40] Samira: That aligns. We'll provision a POC plan for 2 weeks of benchmarking, then a short rollout canary.
[09:48] Priya: Action items for us: send SOC2 artifacts, KMS requirements.
[09:54] Maya: We'll also send the eval corpus and sample prompts.
[09:58] Samira: Perfect. I'll recap next steps at the end.
[10:02] [--- Brief pause / technical glitch — call drops for ~20s, rejoin] 
[10:25] Jonas: Back — sorry, small reconnection.
[10:28] Maya: No problem.
[10:32] Jonas: One more technical: if you want to keep using vLLM orchestration, some customers run Redwood as an overlay — talk to us about hybrid approach where you keep vLLM for dev and Redwood for production.
[10:45] Liam: That might be interesting.
[10:48] Maya: Any gotchas around model tokenization differences? We saw some tokenization-induced deltas before.
[10:54] Jonas: Tokenization differences can cause surface deltas; part of the eval is tokenization alignment. We'll flag mismatches and often provide prompt rewrites or tokenizer harmonization.
[11:06] Priya: For key management — do you rotate keys automatically? We have quarterly rotation policy.
[11:11] Jonas: We support rotation; for BYOK with HSM Private, rotation policies can be driven by your KMS. We also support periodic rotation for provider keys.
[11:22] Maya: Are there any SLA credits if latency SLOs are missed?
[11:26] Samira: Yes, SLA credits are part of the enterprise contract for Dedicated. We'll include details in the SLA appendix.
[11:33] Liam: Operational question: what metrics will you expose for us to monitor?
[11:37] Jonas: Per-route token throughput, latency histograms, model cache hit rates, and error traces. Also per-user cost breakdown.
[11:45] Maya: That sounds good.
[11:47] Samira: Ok quick recap and next steps: 1) Samira sends Dedicated pricing + SKUs and anonymized case study; 2) Jonas shares benchmark harness and POC checklist; 3) Priya sends SOC2 artifacts and key requirements; 4) Aperture sends eval corpus and sample traces; 5) schedule POC kickoff week of 2026-04-20. We'll target a 2-week benchmark window.
[12:12] Maya: Thanks, let's do it.
[12:15] Priya: Thanks everyone.
[12:17] Samira: Thank you — I’ll follow up with calendar invites and links.
[12:22] [Call ends]
